title: The School of Athens
caption:
Ancient Athens. Famous faces.

Raphael was about 26 when he painted this wall in the Vatican, and he filled ancient Greece with the stars of his own Rome. Plato probably wears Leonardo's face. The brooding man on the steps is widely read as Michelangelo, and he isn't in Raphael's full-size drawing at all. Euclid is said to be Bramante, the Pope's architect. And far right, in a black beret, Raphael looks straight back at you.

Swipe for the who's who, then watch the reel: we flew straight up the steps into the painting.

Save this for your next Vatican visit.

slides.alt: Close crop of Plato pointing up and Aristotle gesturing down at the centre of the School of Athens, surrounded by philosophers.

slides.headline: The School of Athens
slides.alt: The whole fresco in its lunette: a vaulted classical hall filled with philosophers on marble steps.

slides.headline: 26 years old.
slides.alt: Big number 26 beside Raphael's Uffizi self-portrait, a young man in a black beret, on a cream paper slide.

slides.headline: Plato wears Leonardo's face.
slides.alt: Leonardo's red-chalk presumed self-portrait beside Raphael's bearded Plato pointing upward.

slides.headline: The brooder is Michelangelo.
slides.alt: Heraclitus slumped against a marble block, chin on fist, writing, in heavy boots.

slides.headline: He wasn't in the plan.
slides.alt: Raphael's preparatory cartoon in Milan with an empty space on the steps, above the same area of the fresco where Heraclitus now sits.

slides.headline: Euclid is the Pope's architect.
slides.alt: Euclid, bald and bent over a slate with a compass, surrounded by young students; a gold marker rings his head.

slides.headline: More regulars on the steps
slides.alt: Four tall cut-up panels: Socrates gesturing, Pythagoras writing, Diogenes sprawled on the steps, and the figure in white.

slides.headline: One man is looking at you.
slides.alt: Small full fresco with a gold leader line to a large circular zoom of Raphael's self-portrait in a black beret at the far right edge.

slides.headline: Now step inside.
slides.alt: Phone frame showing the first frame of our flythrough film: the vaulted hall with Plato and Aristotle on the steps.

notes: Identifications (Leonardo/Plato, Michelangelo/Heraclitus, Bramante/Euclid) are traditional and hedged in copy; Raphael self-portrait is stated by the Vatican Museums. Hypatia explicitly framed as unknown. Heraclitus-late evidence (intonaco, absent from cartoon) per WGA and Wikipedia; worded 'suggests'. Age 26 is approximate (born 1483, wall begun c.1509). Cartoon panel is an approximate match of the same area, not pixel-registered.
